meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('something') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'воленный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fired, dismissed').

examples.text: Ты не уволена, я просто пошутила.
examples.trans: You are not fired, I was simply joking.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

пошутить.gloss: to joke, to make a joke

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шутить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to joke', forming an aspectual pair with 'шутить'.

examples.text: Я смотрю, вы легковерный! Я же пошутила!
examples.trans: I see you're gullible! I was only joking!
Don't be offended, I was only joking.

examples.text: Может быть, шеф просто неудачно пошутил?
examples.trans: Maybe the chef was just joking unsuccessfully?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('horrible, terrible').

examples.trans: What a horrible person you are!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'feeling, emotion, sense' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович испытывает к вам чувства.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich has feelings for you.

examples.text: Ты же знаешь мои настоящие чувства.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'humor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне без хорошего чувства юмора работать просто невозможно.
examples.trans: In our kitchen it is simply impossible to work without a good sense of humor.

examples.text: Гости оценили тонкий юмор шефа и с удовольствием заказали десерт.
examples.trans: The guests appreciated the chef's subtle humor and gladly ordered dessert.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to intend', forming an aspectual pair with 'собраться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to gather, to get ready') (pack or assemble) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: возвращаться домой = to come back home; к + dative = to someone

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.
examples.trans: Remember: evil always comes back to the ruler.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

творить.gloss: to do, to perpetrate; to create

meanings.en: to do, to get up to (something outrageous)
meanings.note: colloquial: что вы творите? = what are you doing?
Secondary conversational sense ('to create') (elevated) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Он сам не понимает, что творит.
examples.trans: He doesn't know what he is doing himself.

examples.text: Самсоновы, вы что творите? Хватит, я прошу вас!
examples.trans: Samsonovs, what are you doing? Stop it, I beg you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'выпендриваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'show off'.

examples.trans: Well, you showed off and that is enough.

examples.text: Ну, немного повыпендривалась перед гостями — и хватит.
examples.trans: Well, you showed off a bit in front of the guests, and that is enough.

examples.text: Макс всегда любит повыпендриваться красивой подачей блюда.
examples.trans: Max always likes to show off with a flashy presentation of a dish.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Secondary conversational sense ('that's enough!') (хватит!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

examples.text: Хватит спорить из-за пустяков, давайте лучше спокойно работать!
examples.trans: Enough arguing over trifles, let us just work calmly instead!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'so'.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to throw; to leave (someone)', paired with 'бросать'.

meanings.en: to leave, to walk out on (someone)
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('to leave, to walk out on (someone)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'made' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: The dish is made according to the rules.
This is an item made by a master's hands.

examples.text: Это блюдо сделано по всем правилам.
examples.trans: This dish is made according to all rules.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'силие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'effort' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Макс приложил огромное усилие, чтобы вовремя закончить все блюда.
examples.trans: Max made a huge effort to finish all the dishes on time.

examples.text: Только общими усилиями всей команды мы спасём сегодняшний вечер.
examples.trans: Only through the joint efforts of the whole team will we save tonight's service.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'купать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to buy', forming an aspectual pair with 'купить'.

meanings.en: to bribe, to buy someone off (fig.)
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('to bribe, to buy someone off (fig.)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('plush, teddy').

examples.text: Ты сама покупала эти плюшевые диваны!
examples.trans: You bought these plush sofas yourself!

examples.text: Ты же сама выбирала эти мягкие плюшевые диваны!
examples.trans: You chose these soft plush sofas yourself!

examples.text: Костя подарил Насте большого плюшевого медведя на праздник.
examples.trans: Kostya gave Nastya a big plush teddy bear for the holiday.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'sofa, couch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is sitting on the sofa.
I will reach the sofa myself.
